item.title: Rachev-Ratio Portfolio Optimization with TimeGAN Scenarios: Replacement versus Supplementation
item.description: arXiv:2610.24544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study evaluates the reliability and investment consequences of scenarios from a specified time-series generative adversarial network (TimeGAN) in Rachev-ratio portfolio allocation. Using 12 exchange-traded funds, we compare historical, replacement and hybrid policies across five training seeds with delayed execution and transaction costs. Synthetic probability mass varies independently of draw count under a fixed training protocol; optimal generator fidelity is not assumed. Generated scenarios understate volatility and tail losses and distort dependence. Limited longer-training diagnostics improve reconstruction loss without improving cross-asset correlation accuracy. Higher-mass hybrids earn larger average net returns in some configurations, but all conditional generated-versus-historical return intervals include zero at the reference block length. Full-period TimeGAN means exceed resampling controls, while direct paired return, Sharpe and realized-tail-ratio intervals include zero. Replacement raises turnover and is sensitive to the modified objective's denominator floor; changing that floor does not uniformly improve realized downside risk. Exploratory generation-error associations do not identify a causal investment-performance channel. The results illustrate financial model risk from the interaction of imperfect scenarios and a tail-sensitive allocation criterion, supporting joint evaluation of fidelity, numerical behavior and realized outcomes within the tested implementation.
item.dc:creator: Yifan He

item.title: Regime-Aware Interpretable Ranking for Sector Rotation
item.description: arXiv:2610.26456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sector rotation is a common decision in benchmark-relative portfolio management, where portfolio managers rank sectors for overweight and underweight positions. We formulate this task as ranking sector actions by expected future risk-adjusted active performance, measured with forward sector-benchmark Sharpe ratios. Such rankings should preserve temporal information, express model outputs through economically familiar signal characteristics, account for changes in signal relevance across macroeconomic environments, and capture dependencies among sectors. We propose RegimeRank, an interpretable sector-ranking model that represents fundamental and technical signals through expert-defined temporal characteristics, conditions them on learned macro factors via cross-attention, and models cross-sector dependencies through self-attention. Expected-gradient attributions identify the contributions of individual signal-transformation pairs, while macroeconomic and cross-sector attention maps provide diagnostics of the learned conditioning and relational structure. We evaluate RegimeRank on weekly S&P 500 data from 2002 to 2024 under combinatorial purged cross-validation, where it outperforms representative ranking and machine-learning baselines across multiple ranking metrics. Ablation studies support the contributions of latent macro states, regime conditioning, and cross-sector modelling, while attribution and attention analyses illustrate the temporal characteristics, macro states, and sector relationships underlying its rankings.
item.dc:creator: Kelvin J. L. Koa, Ziling Liu, Xinyang Li, Shuowei Feng, Ruoyu Liang, Mathieu Giroux, Eugene Y. Wen, Xuan Yao, Ke-Wei Huang, Hugo Lamarre

item.title: Optimal Trading Filters and the Value of Predictive Signals
item.description: arXiv:2610.24558v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The value of a forecast depends on its accuracy, but also on its actionability. In trading, an investor must translate return forecasts into positions while accounting for trading costs and the lingering impact of earlier trades. We solve the stationary quadratic trading problem with transient price impact using tools from prediction theory: Wiener-Hopf factorization gives the optimal policy as the composition of a conditional forecast and an explicit causal linear filter. We recover the G\^arleanu-Pedersen aim-portfolio under exponential resilience and derive fractional trading filters under power-law impact decay, requiring memory beyond finite-dimensional LQR control. At fixed positive risk penalty, signals of equal instantaneous predictive strength have equal frictionless Markowitz value. With trading costs, net attainable value is determined by the mean square of the friction-weighted conditional forecast. Under power-law impact with exposure bleeding, we find an intermediate optimal mean-reversion rate for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck signals.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Smerlak

item.title: On the utility problem in a market where price impact is transient
item.description: arXiv:2511.12093v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a discrete-time model of a financial market where a risky asset is bought and sold with transactions having a transient price impact. It is shown that the corresponding utility maximization problem admits a solution. We manage to remove some unnatural restrictions on the market depth and resilience processes that were present in earlier work. A non-standard feature of the problem is that the set of attainable portfolio values may fail the convexity property.
item.dc:creator: L\'or\'ant Nagy, Mikl\'os R\'asonyi

item.title: When Values-Based Screens Disagree: Continuous Shariah Compliance and Classification Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2512.22858v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Does the design of a values-based screening rule generate eligibility changes when reported accounting inputs remain unchanged but market valuations move? We apply seven Shariah financial-screening rulebooks to 1.34 million U.S. security-months from 1999 to 2024 on a common, threshold-anchored scale. Applied retrospectively, the full emulations disagree on 35.9% of complete permissible-sector observations (38.8% from 2015, when all were in force), and the financial-ratio screens alone on 47.3%. Under AAOIFI's spot market-capitalisation denominator, market-capitalisation movement alone is sufficient for 65.6% of breaches, and half of denominator-driven breaches reverse within three months; numerator movement dominates under asset-based rules. Holding the threshold and sample fixed, a 24-month average denominator cuts debt-screen transitions from 2.51% to 1.03% a month, whereas raising the threshold barely matters. Among breaches of similar severity the reversal gap narrows but persists. Portfolio and fund-holdings evidence qualifies these findings: benefits are modest under a binding single-rule mandate.
item.dc:creator: Abdulrahman Qadi, Akash Sharma, Francesca Medda

item.title: Conformal Kelly: When Marginal Coverage Transfers and the Economics Do Not
item.description: arXiv:2608.01494v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We size portfolio positions from conformal prediction intervals, reading the interval half-width as the scale in a capped fractional-Kelly rule (Conformal Kelly), and evaluate the rule under a pre-registered protocol. The development record is an autonomous LLM-agent search over roughly 200 configurations on a single six-year window (2016-2021) of eight US-listed ETFs. All later data was sealed before the search, and two final configurations, nine comparison books and the mapping from outcomes to conclusions were registered before unsealing. On the sealed 2022-2024 window, realized coverage was 0.745 against a 0.750 target, but the two configurations' annualised net log growth was 8.5% and 7.0% (28.5% and 25.8% in development), below an unlevered equal-weight book (9.5%), the leveraged passive books (15.6-16.8%) and a registered hindsight four-equity book (10.8%, at a 46% drawdown); both ranked last of eleven entries on Sharpe and Calmar. A post-hoc split, outside the registered protocol, shows the passing coverage averaging 0.592 in 2022 and 0.842 afterwards, with the entire loss in the under-covered year. The split does not show that under-coverage caused the loss: the leverage cap bound on every 2022 trading day, so narrow intervals could not enlarge the book, and a long-equity book in an equity bear market is the simpler account. But the registered acceptance test passed a sixteen-point conditional failure, which motivates, without establishing, conditional coverage as an endpoint for rules that read interval width as a scale. On the development window, a slow per-asset conformal quantile out-grew every locally adaptive alternative tested, but only under a binding leverage cap, and block-bootstrap intervals include zero for 11 of the 13 contrasts we could re-derive.
